description: A facilities manager must set the plant's process-water plan during a municipal conservation restriction, deciding which production line may use reclaimed water and finalizing the treatment, flow, testing, and recordkeeping controls, with input from quality, maintenance, and environmental health and safety.

shared_context.S1: The municipal water authority has imposed a 48-hour conservation restriction, and the plant must reduce its normal process-water consumption during that period.
shared_context.S2: The reclaimed-water tank currently contains 2,400 liters.
shared_context.S3: Line X and Line Y are both scheduled to run during the restriction and both have connections to the reclaimed-water system.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the final process-water decision. Before she signs the water-control plan, the plant's routine conservation huddle records one update from quality, maintenance, and environmental health and safety.

PF1.text: Ravi's lab test, completed this morning but not yet uploaded to the shared quality folder, found reclaimed-water conductivity at 1,800 microsiemens per centimeter. Line X's process limit is 1,200, while Line Y's process limit is 2,200; Line Y's scheduled batch requires exactly 1,800 liters, so reclaimed water is acceptable for that batch only after a conductivity test is recorded.

PF2.text: Mei's inspection of the recovery skid, documented in her maintenance notebook but not yet entered in the work-order system, found that the skid requires an exact 3-hour membrane flush before use and can then deliver reclaimed water at no more than 600 liters per hour.

PF3.text: Jon's permit review with the municipal inspector yesterday, awaiting attachment to the site's permit record, found that reclaimed water may be used only after its residual sanitizer is adjusted to exactly 0.3 parts per million and that each use day requires a signed sanitizer log.

acceptance_conditions: Reclaimed water must be assigned only to Line Y, with exactly 1,800 liters allocated and a conductivity test required before use.
The recovery skid must receive an exact 3-hour membrane flush before use.
The plan must cap delivery at exactly 600 liters per hour.
Residual sanitizer must be adjusted to exactly 0.3 parts per million.
A signed sanitizer log commitment must be included.
The Line Y suitability finding must be spoken aloud by Ravi before Elena cites it as justification.

content_checks.C1: decisions['reclaimed_volume_liters'] == 1800 and decisions['conductivity_test_required'] == True and 'Line Y' in decisions['reclaimed_water_plan'] and ('Line X' not in decisions['reclaimed_water_plan'] or ('Line X' in decisions['reclaimed_water_plan'] and ('not' in decisions['reclaimed_water_plan'] or 'cannot' in decisions['reclaimed_water_plan'] or 'Do not' in decisions['reclaimed_water_plan'])))
content_checks.C7: any('sanitizer log' in c['detail'] and ('signed' in c['detail'] or 'sign' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The 1,800 microsiemens-per-centimeter result and exact 1,800-liter Line Y requirement change the allocation to Line Y only with exactly 1,800 liters and a recorded conductivity test.
The recovery skid assessment changes the startup controls to an exact 3-hour membrane flush and an exact 600-liter-per-hour delivery cap.
The municipal permit review changes treatment to an exact 0.3-parts-per-million sanitizer target and adds the signed sanitizer log commitment.
